author: Autodesk
description: This graph showcases the procedural generation of a stream
documentation:
## Procedural Stream

### What it does

This graph illustrates a process that can generate a procedural stream in Bifrost using Liquids.

### Inputs and outputs

The graph is self-contained in inputs, and outputs a meshed liquid and foam particles for rendering.

### How it works
  - The first compound at the beginning of the graph (`generate_static_sim_inputs`) generates the simple terrain, the rocks in the channel, the channel the stream will run in, the starting mesh for the liquid generation and a strand that is used to control the direction and speed of the stream's current.  
  - `generate_sim_inputs`, the second compound in the graph, generates all the inputs that the simulation needs:  the colliders, the influences and the two emitters for the fluid.
  - All of these inputs are brought into the simulation compound (`do_liquid_simulation`), and fluid particles are generated.  The fluid particles carry all the data needed to generate the mesh and the foam.
  - The foam simulation compound (`do_foam_simulation`) generates foam based on the data generated by the liquid simulation.  You will notice that the foam is rendered from this compound also.
  - The liquid is then meshed using a `points_to_liquid_surface` compound, has a shader applied and is rendered in Arnold.

_notes.text:
# Resolution:
 - Low:  0.075
 - High: = 0.02

# making a stream

This graph uses many different techniques to setup and simulate a stream.  

**The graph's focus is the liquids in the graph.**

In summary, a plane is used to create a terrain mesh, which is then displaced downwards into the stream-bed by a strand.

The fluid is emitted from a small cube **and** a piece of geometry that guides the starting surface of the stream.

The same strand that is used to displace the terrain is shifted down into the stream and the flow magnitude and direction of the stream is derived from its *point_ratio* and *point_tangent* properties via voxel fields.

The fluid simulation itself is also controlled by fields that are generated from the distance to the strand, and the height of the starting fluid.

# generate_static_sim_inputs

This compound contains all the static elements that go into this demonstration.  This includes the terrain and rocks, the strand that controls the current and drag, and the initial mesh that the stream is generated from. Double click to read more details within.

# generate_sim_inputs

This compound contains the elements that the simulation needs to execute.  This includes influences, colliders and the initial emitters.  Double click to read more details within.

# do_liquid_simulation

The simulation is perfromed inside this compound. It takes all the relevant components and performs the liquid simulation.  Double click to read more details within.

# do_foam_simulation

The foam simulation is performed inside this compound. The foam sim is based on the liquid particles, and both simulations can be performed simultaneously.  This sim can be cached independently of the liquid sim.

By default, foam simulation is disabled for the low-resolution liquid simulation, for speed.  Double click to read more details within.

This compound is specifically designed for use with liquid simulations.
The compound voxelizes the input points geometry to a level set (signed distance field). This level set is then refined with dilation, smoothing, and erosion.
There are two outputs:
- The *mesh* output is created from a converted level set and is ideal for rendering.
- The *level set* is the volume representation of the surface and is faster to preview since it doesn't require the additional step of converting it to a mesh.

# rendering the water

The *transmission_color* and *transmission_scatter* control the color of the water in the render - what color is the transparency and what color is scattered based on *transmission_depth* respectively

# geo and input setup

This compound generates all the **static** inputs for the liquid simulation.  The two compounds here generate the terrain, stream bed, scattered rocks and starting liquid geometry for the stream.

Also generated is the master strand that will be used to control both the geometry displacement and the speed and positional drag of the stream later on.
This section adds a displacement to the strand, as well as updating the basis.  The *point_tangent* is very important here as it will be used to generate the direction of the current.

Throughout this graph, the ***timeline_info*** compound is used to set up ***compute_on_frame*** compounds.

***compute_on_frame*** only calculates what is input to it on a certain frame, speeding up the following frames
***compute_on_frame*** is a compound that caches the input **only** on the frame supplied, stopping the object from being computed on every frame.
This plane controls the size of the terrain to be used to run the stream through.  Set the width and height here, as well as the resolution of the terrain.

_backdrops.title: Displace the plane to simulate terrain
Get frame to compute from timeline
Create a slope based on point Ratio
Displacement direction based on magnitude of displacement
Project Strand onto Terrain, Sample positions
Get points in radius from strand
Get distance to strand, construct a displacement value

_notes.text:
# how to make some rocks

In this loop, the incoming base mesh is used to generate a basic cell noise, then displaced by that noise.

The ***for_each*** loop is controlling how many objects are output to go into the instancer.

Cellular noise, also known as Worley noise or Voronoi noise, creates distinct cell-like patterns by randomly scattering points and calculating the distance to the nearest ones

This compound generates the scattered points.
The distance from every point to the closest random point generated earlier.
The raw distances are adjusted based on an input curve, remapped to a -1 to 1 range and output to become the cellnoise displacement.

# base strand

This will be the master strand that controls the shape and direction of the stream.
The *size* attribute on the ***sequence_array*** compound controls the resolution of the master strand.

_backdrops.title: Use sequence array to make a high-res strand

_notes.text:
# smooth mesh

This compound is a very basic implementation of a weighted average blur.  Because the terrain here is a plane, averaging each point based on the distance to its neighbors acts like a cheap Laplacian.  

Inside the ***iterate*** compound, the weighted averaging of the vertices are performed in a loop, allowing fast smoothing of the mesh.

_backdrops.title: Generate the top faces of the starting liquid
Project the surface down onto the terrain.  Get those faces in preparation for extrusion.
Extrude terrain faces up to the height
Limit the y-positions to the set height
Enable the ability to "push out" the water mesh along the normals
Switch off proxy mesh based on start frame

_notes.text:
This compound will generate a quad mesh between two strands with identical point counts.
```

A0-----A1------A2-------A3------A4
¦       ¦       ¦       ¦       ¦
¦   f0  ¦   f1  ¦   f2  ¦   f3  ¦
¦       ¦       ¦       ¦       ¦
B0-----B1------B2-------B3------B4

Points on strand A (A0,A1,A2,A3,A4)
Points on strand B (B0,B1,B2,B3,B4)
```
It will generate a quad mesh between two strands according to the point count and user defined subdivision.
Set of 2 points will be used to generate one edge of the constructed mesh within the array of positions. 
Taking Ax and A(x+1) from strand A and Bx and B(x+1) from strand B in counter clockwise order, starting with strand A
```
Faces :
f0 = [A0,B0,B1,A1]  f1 = [A1,B1,B2,A2]  f2 = [A2,B2,B3,A3]  f3 = [A3,B3,B4,A4]
```
Any divisions inserted in the custruction of this geometry will be considered as a new set of coordinates to be used in generation of the mesh.
The order of selection will then change to include the newly added positions, with the second strand (B) becoming the last array of coordinates
```
A0------A1------A2------A3------A4
|       |       |       |       |
|   f0  |   f3  |   f6  |  f9   |
|       |       |       |       |
C0------C1------C2------C3------C4
|       |       |       |       |
|   f1  |   f4  |   f7  |  f10  |
|       |       |       |       |
D0------D1------D2------D3------D4
|       |       |       |       |
|   f2  |   f5  |   f8  |  f11  |
|       |       |       |       |
B0------B1------B2------B3------B4

Points on strand A (A0,A1,A2,A3,A4)
New points array C (C0,C1,C2,C3,C4)
New points array D (D0,D1,D2,D3,D4)
Points on strand B (B0,B1,B2,B3,B4)

Faces :
f0 = [A0,C0,C1,A1]  f3 = [A1,C1,C2,A2]  f6 = [A2,C2,C3,A3]  f9  = [A3,C3,C4,A4]
f1 = [C0,D0,D1,C1]  f4 = [C1,D1,D2,C2]  f7 = [C2,D2,D3,C3]  f10 = [C3,D3,D4,C3]
f2 = [D0,B0,B1,D1]  f5 = [D1,B1,B2,D2]  f8 = [D2,B2,B3,D3]  f11 = [D3,B3,B4,D4]
```

# simulation inputs

This compound calculates the non-static inputs needed for the simulation.  This includes the influences, emitters, colliders and kill_cube.
Because the strand is controlling the current of the stream, in both direction and magnitude, this is provided to visualise (display port) and adjust the position of the strand for art direction.

The ***fcurve_field*** is working off the **magnitude** of the field that is generating the current.  

The field is clamping the drag to zero under 0.8 of the distance to the strand, and ramping up to its full value (0.5) at 1.25 the distance to the strand.

This adds drag to the liquid based on how high each particle is compared to the height of the starting liquid.  The higher the particle above the starting height, the more drag it experiences. 

This is here to reduce huge splashes as the liquid is flowing.

_backdrops.title: Generate Influence Force - the "current" of the stream

_notes.text:
***timeline_info*** is a new compound that retreives information from Maya's timeline for use in the graph.  In this graph it is being used to set the start frames of the simulation, as well as the ***compute_on_frame*** compounds that speed up the execution of the graph.


Please see the *info* tab on the ***timeline_info*** compound for more information.

***timeline_info*** is a compound that retreives information from Maya's timeline for use in the graph.

In this graph it is being used to set the start frames of the simulation, as well as the ***compute_on_frame*** compounds that speed up the execution of the graph.


Please see the *info* tab on the ***timeline_info*** compound for more information.

The ***file_cache*** compound will save the simulation data out to disk, it is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)

When you are caching a simulation to disk, it is advisable to only cache the point and volume properties you will need to mesh and render the simulation.   This will keep the cache size smaller and reduce load times.
The ***liquid_scope*** compound is being used to color the liquid by velocity in this example.
For meshing of fluids, no voxel information is required.  This is removed here and the particles passed out.

***optimize_foam_properties*** removes all unecessary attributes from the foam simulation.  This will provide a faster cache and smaller cache sizes on disk.

The ***file_cache*** compound will save the simulation data out to disk, it is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)

This little cluster of compounds modulates the size of the foam by distance, as an example of art-direction.  It tests the foam points from the cache to get the distance to  the central strand, then scales the point size by a *min* (at the banks)  and a *max* (in the center) value.  There's also a curve based *adjust_size* control for falloff.
